Nyirbator Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nyírbátor, Hungary

Not demolished. Nyírbátor's Jewish cemetery, dated by its oldest tombstone to 1852, appears to remain active even today - its most recent gravestone is dated 2018. The community itself traces to 1754, when six Jewish families lived in the town; it grew steadily, reaching roughly 1,000-1,200 by 1918 and peaking at 1,899 in 1941. The congregation, founded around 1816 by Rabbi Simon Mandel and his five sons, later produced Eduárd Mandel, founder of the city's well-known BÓNI factory. After a schism in Hungarian Jewry in 1867, most of the community remained 'Status Quo,' running three synagogues, a Talmud Torah school, and a burial society by the late 1920s under Chief Rabbi Ábrahám Lemberger. On April 22, 1944, Nyírbátor's Jews were taken to the Nyíregyháza Ghetto, and 20-22 were deported to Auschwitz. Around 491 returned after the war and briefly re-established the community, but all left the city following the 1956 revolution.
